rule: Layers are distinct: the actor-semantic nucleus (transition-form + effect-primitives) is justified by primary actor semantics; the host calculus is assumed from Rust/type theory; Bombay encodings are representation choices classified as required-encoding, preferred-encoding, derived-combinator, or policy. Semantic status is primitive/derived/extension/not-applicable. Public API status is retain/reclassify/redesign/remove/not-public.

actor_semantic_nucleus.statement: (behavior state, one typed communication) -> (communications, fresh creation requests, next behavior or stop); one isolated turn per event
a transition may emit finitely many communications to known recipients; unordered across the transition's effect set
a transition may request creation of actors at addresses fresh with respect to the configuration; creation never overwrites
a transition designates the behavior used for the next communication; replacement is distinct from allocation

nucleus_note: N-fold is the TRANSITION-FORM: (behavior, communication) -> effects + next behavior. It is not a fourth effect alongside send/create/become. N-send, N-create, N-become are EFFECT-PRIMITIVES: the three primitive effect forms available in the transition result. Termination is NOT an actor-model primitive: Agha's actors persist (FMOODS 2002 persistence discipline). Bombay's Step::Stop is a typed extension — model-level inertness is become-to-sink; the explicit stop verdict exists to signal reclamation to the interpreter. It is classified bombay-derived extension, not law.

primitives.name: One-communication fold
primitives.rust_type: trait Behavior { fn init; fn step } + trait State::handle (crates/behavior/src/behavior.rs:389-431)
primitives.formation_rule: A behavior is a total deterministic fold from exactly one typed Event to Result<Actions, Error>; init runs before mailbox events.
primitives.operational_semantics: One isolated turn: consume one event, produce the complete effect product as data; determinism = function of message history.
laws: One communication at a time (Agha 1986; De Koster-De Meuter 2025 Isolated Turn; Clinger 1981 arrival events)
Deterministic function of the received message sequence (AMST 1997)
Behavior domain equation F ~= [M -> (F x P(A x M))] (Clinger 1981)

evidence: core.rs drives single events and asserts complete Actions values

primitives.name: Explicit termination verdict
primitives.formation_rule: A transition may return the stop verdict, signaling end of life to the interpreter.
primitives.operational_semantics: Stop is final; the interpreter reaps. Model-level inertness would be become-to-sink; the explicit verdict carries the exit value.
laws: Stop is terminal and total per fold
derivable_from: N-become (inert sink) plus an interpreter-visible signal
primitives.retention_constraint: project policy: explicit typed termination for reclamation and lifecycle reporting; NOT an Agha primitive (persistence discipline, FMOODS 2002)

attempts.approach: Model termination as becoming an inert sink behavior
attempts.code_summary: sink = rec(b.behavior ignoring all messages) (AMST 1997 defines exactly this sink)
attempts.obstruction: Derivation SUCCEEDS semantically: inertness is expressible. Retention of Stop is a Bombay policy: an explicit terminal verdict gives the interpreter a typed reclamation signal and Exit value that a sink cannot distinguish from a live behavior

eliminability.rationale: Termination is semantically derivable (sink); the explicit verdict is a retained representation, classified Bombay extension/policy — not a model primitive.
eliminability.mechanical_probe: semantic derivation via AMST sink; retained as representation by policy

limitations: Explicit termination is a Bombay policy extension; Agha's actors persist
A sink behavior cannot signal reclamation to the interpreter
Exit value semantics are interpreter-defined

Identity: a wrapper over a behavior with none of the wrapper's events reduces to the inner behavior up to lane widening
